title: Browser build: pr-ci.yml does not build from latest dev commits.
body: **Input:** - see screenprint *Output:* - 3.4.2.3-dev/aaps-3.4.2.3-dev-pul-4896-merge.apk *Expected output:* - 4.0.0-dev-a/aaps-4.0.0-dev-pul-4896-merge.apk **Additional info:** Version validation falls back to latest release version when BRANCH_NAME is not numeric version? - name: Extract VERSION run: | BRANCH_NAME=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD) if echo "$BRANCH_NAME" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$'; then VERSION="$BRANCH_NAME" else VERSION=$(grep 'val appVersion' buildSrc/src/main/kotlin/Versions.kt | awk -F '"' '{print $2}') fi echo "VERSION=$VERSION" >> $GITHUB_ENV **Screen print:**

comments.body:
@vanelsberg 

Because PR #4896 will be merged into the dev3 branch, after the merge it will use the Versions.kt from dev3, so the output being version v3 is correct.![Screenshot_20260617_121624~2.jpg](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a07d596-3b77-44fc-8804-be4a253bcf6b)

@Angus-repo 
> Because PR https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/pull/4896 will be merged into the dev3 branch...

Intended target of the PR is not relevant?

I explicitly set to merge the PR per with the *dev* branch. So it merges (at least it should) with latest dev-bits, not a version tag. And current version of latest dev bit is 4.0.0dev-a. *Not 3.4.2.3-dev* ?

I think behavior of pr-ci should be analog to "Branch CI": I should be able to merge a PR with any branch (even when it could fail to merge)

> slight misunderstanding...

Ah, true. After further inspection of the .yml I see how it is working. It merges the PR with the target branch.
That is ok. Prevents problems as you mentioned.

But then my next question: 
Why present the user to select any branch name for the PR. This confused me, thinking I could merge on any branch (which is theoretically possible but unwanted in most cases).

Maybe it should error and alert the user: "This PR can not be merged with the branch selected..."?
This option is a menu that is always present in the GitHub Actions interface. I had looked for a way to hide it before, but it does not seem possible.

Ok, no real issue then.
Thanks for the info. Will close this issue 👍
